title: Xbash_Ransomware_Incident_Response_Scenario_bdf
description: Investigate the Xbash ransomware incident, identify indicators of compromise, and contain the threat.
outcomes: Identify indicators of compromise (IOCs) such as IP addresses, network ports, and exfiltrated files.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has been compromised by the Xbash ransomware. This malware combines ransomware, coinmining, and self-propagation capabilities, targeting both Linux and Windows systems. Your task is to investigate the incident, identify the indicators of compromise, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter the word 'start' to begin the scenario.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

Enter the word 'start' to begin the scenario.

levels.title: Identify the External Host
levels.content:
Identify the external host communicating with the compromised system.

Question: What is the IP address of the command-and-control server that the ransomware is communicating with?
levels.solution: Investigate network connections and logs to find suspicious outbound connections. The IP address of the command-and-control server is 192.168.90.5. This is an IP address flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate network connections and logs to find suspicious outbound connections. Useful commands include: netstat -tuln, ss -tulnp, lsof -i -P -n | grep ESTABLISHED.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port
levels.content:
Determine which network port is used for suspicious command-and-control communication.

Question: What network port is the ransomware using to communicate with the command-and-control server?
levels.solution: Examine network traffic and service logs to identify unusual port usage. The network port used is 4443. This is a port number flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine network traffic and service logs to identify unusual port usage. Useful commands include: netstat -tuln, ss -tulnp, lsof -i -P -n | grep ESTABLISHED.

levels.title: Identify Exfiltrated Files
levels.content:
Identify files or datasets that were transferred outside the environment before encryption.

Question: What files were exfiltrated from the victim host to an external server?
levels.solution: Analyze logs and network traffic to determine what data was sent out of the network. The files exfiltrated are quarterly_report.txt, employee_data.csv, and passwords.txt. These are file path flags.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze logs and network traffic to determine what data was sent out of the network. Useful commands include: grep -r 'exfil' /var/log/, journalctl -xe, tcpdump -i any -w exfil.pcap.
